title: An exact match beats widening

blocks.text: When no overload takes exactly the argument's type, Java widens it: an `int` can go to a `double` parameter. So if an `int` overload is missing, an `int` argument quietly reaches the `double` one, and the program compiles, but means something else.
An `Integer` argument unboxes to `int`, so `area(Integer.valueOf(4))` is a square too.

cases.says: A circle's and a rectangle's areas are right.
area(4) is 16.0: the int overload is an exact match, not a circle.
area(100000) is 1.0E10: the side is widened before it is squared.

concepts: An exact match is chosen over a widening one, so a missing int overload silently sends an int to a double one.
